 Tropical cyclones Very severe cyclone Arnab nears Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast ahead of October 28 landfall, India
 By Rishav Kothari 
 Tuesday, October 27, 2026 12:45 UTC Tuesday, October 27, 2026 12:45 UTC Very severe cyclonic storm Arnab approached India’s Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast on October 27, 2026, with landfall forecast near Yanam during the morning of October 28. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecast landfall winds of 125–135 km/h (78–84 mph), gusting to 150 km/h (93 mph), alongside storm surge and isolated extremely heavy rainfall. 
 Image credit: KMA/GEO-KOMPSAT/RAMMB/CIRA,The Watchers
 At 08:30 IST (03:00 UTC) on October 27, IMD located Arnab about 220 km (137 miles) south-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 240 km (149 miles) east-southeast of Kakinada. Estimated sustained winds were 140–150 km/h (87–93 mph), gusting to 165 km/h (103 mph), and the cyclone was moving west-northwest at 20 km/h (12 mph).
 Advisory No. 10, issued at 10:30 IST (05:00 UTC), forecast a west-northwestward track through the evening of October 27, followed by a northwestward turn. IMD expected the cyclone to cross between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, close to Yanam, by 11:30 IST (06:00 UTC) on October 28.
 IMD’s National Bulletin 17, issued at 12:40 IST (07:10 UTC), forecast further offshore strengthening to 150–160 km/h (93–99 mph), gusting to 180 km/h (112 mph), during October 27, followed by weakening before landfall. Further rapid weakening was expected after the cyclone moved inland.
 Cyclone Arnab observed and forecast track. Credit: IMD Isolated extremely heavy rainfall was forecast across coastal Andhra Pradesh and southern Odisha on October 27 and 28. The inland rainfall threat included isolated heavy to very heavy rain in eastern Telangana and isolated extremely heavy rain in southern Chhattisgarh on October 28.
 Storm surge of 1–2 m (3.3–6.6 feet) above astronomical tide is forecast during landfall, with the highest surge expected near Kakinada and Yanam, which is part of the Union Territory of Puducherry. The surge was expected to flood low-lying coastal areas; the forecast height is above the predicted tide, not a uniform flood depth above ground.
 Cyclone Arnab forecast track with cone of uncertainty. Credit: IMD The coastal bulletin issued at 14:15 IST (08:45 UTC) on October 27 kept Great Danger Signal No. X at Kakinada port and No. IX at Visakhapatnam, Gangavaram and Bheemunipatnam. Great Danger Signal No. VIII remained hoisted at Machilipatnam and Nizampatnam, while the bulletin forecast high to very high seas along the Andhra Pradesh coast.
 IMD warned of potential damage to vulnerable houses, power and communication lines, trees and crops. Urban, river and coastal flooding and landslides in hilly areas were among the hazards identified in its national bulletin.
 Fishermen were advised not to venture into the west-central Bay of Bengal or waters along and off the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts from October 27 to 29.
 Cyclone Arnab storm surge forecast map. Credit: IMD Cyclone Arnab storm surge forecast table. Credit: IMD The National Crisis Management Committee reviewed preparations across Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Telangana, Chhattisgarh and Puducherry on October 26. According to the Press Information Bureau, authorities had arranged shelters and evacuation measures and activated district control rooms.
 The National Disaster Response Force told the committee that teams had been deployed, with additional teams on standby. Rescue and relief personnel from the Army, Navy, Air Force and Indian Coast Guard, together with ships and aircraft, had been kept ready.
 The same October 26 statement said the Coast Guard had guided multiple vessels to shore and alerted remaining vessels to return.
 Odisha’s Chief Minister’s Office announced on October 24 that schools, colleges and Anganwadi centers in Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri districts would close on October 28 and 29. District collectors were authorized to decide closures elsewhere.
 The announcement said 302 rescue teams had been kept ready and instructed officials to arrange evacuations from low-lying areas and transfers of pregnant women and patients to healthcare facilities. IMD advised residents in vulnerable coastal housing to move to safer places and follow official evacuation and traffic instructions.
 References:
 1 Tropical Cyclone Advisory No. 10 – RSMC New Delhi / IMD – October 27, 2026
 2 National Bulletin No. 17 – IMD – October 27, 2026
